answer: An agent market called juniper could admit identities to its grove registry only after each locks 100 USDC in a separate escrow for 30 days. The registry verifies deposits on-chain and rejects reuse of an escrow, so a Sybil spiral ties up another 100 USDC per identity, imposing capital and opportunity costs. This limits cheap identity creation, but wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, and refundable stakes do not prove honest behavior.
